description:
FILED s526w1 (Opus, 2026-10-24) from the URI-5.34 board census (t/query.t row 32).  SILENT WRONG, PRE-EXISTING (main 761d92f4 gives the same).

A scalar VARIABLE holding a BLESSED reference, copied into a NEW array element (an anon array `[$x]`, a list assignment `@a = ($x)`, push), is stored as the variable's own BOX -- an alias -- so a later assignment to the variable changes the element.

REPRO (scratch/s526w1/pr/wrap3.pl):
    my $p = [1]; my @a = ($p); $p = 8; print "1 ", ref($a[0]), "\n";
    my $s = bless {}, 'K'; my $t = [$s]; $s = 8; print "4 ", ref($t->[0]), "\n";
    my $o = bless {}, 'K'; my $r = $o; my @b = ($r); $r = 8; print "5 ", ref($b[0]), "\n";
  perl 5.40.3: 1 ARRAY / 4 K / 5 K
  PCL: 1 ARRAY / 4 (empty) / 5 (empty)
  and `$v = [$v]` with a blessed $v makes the element the new array itself (URI::_query::query_form's
  `$vals = [_is_array($vals) ? @$vals : $vals]` -> "?c=ARRAY(0x1)").

THE MECHANISM (read, not yet changed): cl/pcl-runtime.lisp %p-array-store-scalar's arm
    ;; Blessed box: preserve as-is (class must not be lost)
    ((p-box-class item) (%p-vpush item arr))
stores ITEM itself.  The class is carried on the box, and the VARIABLE's box carries it too after
`my $s = bless ...` (box-set copies it), so the arm cannot tell a variable from a referent and aliases
the variable.  An unblessed reference takes the `(make-p-box inner)` copy arm and is right.  The fix is
a fresh container with the value AND the class (and the is-ref flag, cf. %p-glob-container-copy) --
but read first why "as-is" was chosen (a later re-bless through one copy must be seen by the others:
in perl the blessing is on the REFERENT), and check the hash arm (%p-make-hash-entry) for the same rule.

PROBABLY THE SAME MECHANISM: #3557 (Path-Tiny filesystem.t: `while (my $x = $it->()) { push @d, $x }`
over Path::Tiny OBJECTS leaves @d holding the loop variable's last, false value -- the objects are
blessed).  Run #3557's repro against the fix.

=== DONE (s529a) ===
Fixed in s529a commit 75f3cdb1 (2026-10-31, Opus).  %p-array-store-scalar's "blessed box: preserve as-is" and "scalar ref: as-is" arms stored the VARIABLE's box; every reference now takes %p-ref-container-copy = %p-container-snapshot (same referent + class + is-ref), also the hash arm's glob copy (was %p-glob-container-copy).  A blessed PLAIN scalar (a bless \$x referent) copies its value, unblessed.  Probes scratch/s529a/pr/b1-b3 (46 lines) = perl except the re-bless-through-a-copy rows (#4000) and a blessed qr element (#4001), both filed.  Guard Pl/t/blessed-copy-01.t (4 rows; 1, 2, 4 fail on 77c7d9d7).  ir-spec §2.6.  Board rows out by edit (one-file runs): URI query.t 32; Pod-Simple fcodes_l 41, pulltitl 36, html01 *PLAN*, html03 *FILE*, puller *FILE* (135/135 now), x_nixer 3, xhtml10 62; Path-Tiny filesystem.t 39 40 47 48 (#3557); HTTP-Message response.t *PLAN* (the file now reaches row 66 = #3828).  Gate PASS 338 / 11,489; sweep TOTAL 18,761 +0; corpus-diff identical.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a variable holding a BLESSED ref, copied into a new array element ([$x], @a = ($x), push), is stored as the variable box itself -- a later assignment to the variable changes the element (URI query.t 32; probably #3557)
